_verified_against.retroarch: libretro/RetroArch master eb7335f939c39be703662c2a0e07c106f99b64ac (version.all 1.22.2); remap semantics identical at tag v1.22.2

_ids_notes: 0-15 are RETRO_DEVICE_ID_JOYPAD_* (libretro.h). 16-23 are RetroArch's RARCH_ANALOG_*_PLUS/MINUS (input/input_defines.h, RARCH_FIRST_CUSTOM_BIND = 16). Y+ is down, Y- is up (autoconfig labels l_y_minus 'LS Up'). In memory 'unmapped' is RARCH_UNMAPPED = 1024; in a .rmp it is written and read as -1.
positional_convention: The RetroPad is SNES-positional: B = south, A = east, Y = west, X = north (libretro.h comments on RETRO_DEVICE_ID_JOYPAD_*). L/R are bumpers, L2/R2 triggers, L3/R3 stick clicks.
_physical_notes: Holds only when the active autoconfig profile is positional. Both shipped Steam virtual pad profiles are (sdl2/Steam Virtual Gamepad.cfg: input_b_btn=0 = SDL south; udev/Steam Input x-box.cfg: input_b_btn=0 = BTN_SOUTH). guide, misc1, paddles, touchpad, trackpads and gyro have no RetroPad id and cannot be the source of a remap.

joypad_ports.semantics: 0-based joypad port that RetroArch user N reads. Default N-1 (config_set_defaults). Two users on one port is allowed; an index past the devices is reassigned to the first free one at load (input_config_sanitize_joypad_indices).
joypad_ports.port_is_sdl_index: With input_joypad_driver = sdl2, port i is SDL device index i: sdl2_joypad_init opens 0..SDL_NumJoysticks()-1 into ports 0..n-1, and a hot-plugged pad takes the index SDL gives it (SDL_JOYDEVICEADDED).
joypad_ports._sdl_order_note: Seen on the owner's Deck (2026-10-22, Flatpak 1.22.2, sdl2 driver, docs/13 S1): users follow js node order and the pads keep their 'Microsoft X-Box 360 pad N' names, which is SDL < 2.30 behaviour. SDL >= 2.30 would sort Steam virtual pads by slot and name them after the physical pad. [VERIFY] the SDL2 the Flatpak bundles.
joypad_ports.overridden_by: core, content-dir and game override .cfg files (config/<core>/*.cfg) save input_playerN_joypad_index when it differs (config_save_overrides); input_device_reservation_type != 0 moves users on connect; input_assign_ports_on_button_press assigns ports dynamically.

remap_file.format: RetroArch config_file (key = "value" lines). Values are quoted integers when RetroArch writes them; config_get_int also accepts unquoted.
remap_file.direction: KEY names the SOURCE (the RetroPad input as produced by autoconfig for user N); VALUE is the RetroPad id the CORE receives. input_player1_btn_b = "8" means pressing RetroPad B sends A to the core.
remap_file.identity_rule: A key that is absent, or whose value equals its own id, is identity. A source remapped away no longer reaches its own id: input_state() drops the original bit when remap_ids[id] != id.
remap_file.swap_rule: Remaps are not swaps. To exchange A and B you must write both input_playerN_btn_a = "0" and input_playerN_btn_b = "8"; writing only one makes two sources drive one target and leaves the other target unreachable.
remap_file.keyboard_keys: input_player{N}_key_{same suffixes as btn/stk} = RETROK_* code (keyboard mapper; not managed by map-helper)
remap_file.button_value_range: 0-15 (button) or 16-23 (drive an analog half-axis at full deflection) or -1 (unmapped). Out-of-range values are clamped to unmapped by input_remapping_load_file.
remap_file.stick_value_range: 16-23 (axis to axis; sign inverted automatically when source and target parity differ) or 0-15 (axis to button above input_axis_threshold) or -1.

per_port_keys.input_libretro_device_p{N}: libretro device id for core port N (RETRO_DEVICE_JOYPAD = 1, RETRO_DEVICE_ANALOG = 5, subclasses = ((index + 1) << 8) | base). Core specific; see cores/*.json device_types.
per_port_keys.input_remap_port_p{N}: 0-based core port that user N feeds. Several users may feed one port. Value > MAX_USERS is reset to N-1; MAX_USERS means 'feeds no port'.
per_port_keys.input_player{N}_analog_dpad_mode: 0 none, 1 left stick, 2 right stick, 3 left forced, 4 right forced, 5 left+right, 6 twinstick, 7 left+right forced, 8 twinstick forced (enum analog_dpad_mode).

remap_file.player_index: N is 1-based and counts RetroArch users (the Port N Controls menu rows), not core ports. Users are routed to core ports by input_remap_port_pN.
remap_file.players_saved: input_remapping_save_file writes users 1..input_max_users plus any user mapped to a port; btn/stk keys only when not identity; -1 only when the core declared a descriptor for that id. device, analog_dpad_mode and remap_port are always written (remap_port is skipped for a port assigned by 'first press').

paths.sort_by_controller: With input_remap_sort_by_controller_enable = true, <library_name> becomes <library_name>/<sanitized display name of user 1's device>.

remap_file.load_order: game, then content_dir, then core. The FIRST file found is loaded and the search stops. Files do not layer: input_remapping_load_file resets every remap to defaults first.
remap_file.save_on_exit: remap_save_on_exit (default true) rewrites the file that was loaded, from memory, when content closes or RetroArch quits.

binding_values_in_cfg._applies_to: retroarch.cfg input_player{N}_* and input_* hotkey binds, and autoconfig files. Values are device-specific indices for the active input_joypad_driver.
binding_values_in_cfg.button: "<n>" = joypad button index from the driver (key suffix _btn)
binding_values_in_cfg.axis: "+<n>" or "-<n>" = axis n positive/negative half (key suffix _axis)
binding_values_in_cfg.keyboard: input_<name> = key name such as "f2" (no suffix); mouse uses _mbtn
binding_values_in_cfg.precedence: A user bind in retroarch.cfg wins; if it is nul / unset the autoconfig profile's bind is used (input_key_pressed in input_driver.c).

steam_virtual_pad_indices._source: retroarch-joypad-autoconfig sdl2/Steam Virtual Gamepad.cfg and udev/Steam Input x-box.cfg (both VID 10462 = 0x28DE, PID 4607 = 0x11FF)
steam_virtual_pad_indices._see_also: hotkeys.json: hotkey key names and the sdl2 driver's button/axis indices, which the hotkey writer uses

sdl2._guide_note: guide = 5 is SDL_CONTROLLER_BUTTON_GUIDE; it is not bound in the shipped profile [VERIFY that Steam forwards it]
